exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. PyTorch stable documentation reviewed 2026-09-19 (current docs identified as 2.14).

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are completed, including required code and table discoveries.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; typed recall and coding questions provide the scored retrieval signal.

authoring_notes: Updated for the learning-v2 renderer. PyTorch code is displayed as syntax-highlighted code_file material with clickable annotations instead of inline prose. Progressive tables are used for shape reasoning and concept comparisons while preserving the existing curriculum scope.

prompts.label: SELECT AN AVAILABLE ACCELERATOR OR CPU
prompts.placeholder: Click the accelerator availability check and fallback.

annotations.title: Check accelerator availability
annotations.explanation: Current PyTorch accelerator APIs can query whether a supported accelerator backend is available.

annotations.title: Get the current accelerator
annotations.explanation: The accelerator API abstracts over supported accelerator backends.

annotations.title: CPU fallback
annotations.explanation: A CPU device keeps the same .to(device) workflow when no accelerator is available.

prompts.label: PUT MODEL AND BATCH ON COMPATIBLE DEVICES
prompts.placeholder: Click model.to and the input/target transfers.

reveal.code:
model = model.to(device)

for X, y in loader:
    X = X.to(device)
    y = y.to(device)

    logits = model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(logits, y)

annotations.title: Move registered model state
annotations.explanation: model.to moves registered Parameters and buffers to the requested device.

annotations.title: Move model inputs
annotations.explanation: Input tensors need their own transfer before they interact with accelerator-resident model parameters.

annotations.title: Move targets when required
annotations.explanation: Loss computation generally needs its tensor operands on compatible devices.

prompts.label: MOVING ONLY ONE SIDE CAUSES ERRORS
prompts.placeholder: What common failure happens if the model is on an accelerator but the batch remains on CPU?

reveal.text: Operations between tensors on incompatible devices commonly fail with a device-mismatch error.

annotations.title: Collect registered model state
annotations.explanation: The state dict contains registered Parameters and persistent buffers.

annotations.title: Persist the state data
annotations.explanation: Saving a state dict is the recommended weights-oriented pattern instead of serializing the entire Python model object.

reveal.code:
import torch

model = Classifier()

state = torch.load(
    "model_weights.pt",
    weights_only=True,
    map_location="cpu",
)

model.load_state_dict(state)
model.eval()

annotations.title: Load the saved mapping
annotations.explanation: torch.load reads the serialized state data. weights_only=True limits loading to weights-oriented objects and is a recommended safety practice.

annotations.title: Weights-oriented loading
annotations.explanation: This narrows what the loader is allowed to reconstruct from the serialized file.

annotations.title: Restore registered module state
annotations.explanation: The model architecture must already exist before the state mapping can be loaded.

annotations.title: Choose the next operating mode explicitly
annotations.explanation: Loading a state dict does not automatically switch the model to evaluation mode.

prompts.label: SAVE ENOUGH STATE TO RESUME TRAINING
prompts.placeholder: Click model, optimizer, epoch, and scheduler state.

reveal.code:
checkpoint = {
    "epoch": epoch,
    "model": model.state_dict(),
    "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
    "scheduler": scheduler.state_dict(),
}

torch.save(checkpoint, "checkpoint.pt")

annotations.title: Training position
annotations.explanation: Store enough progress information to resume at the correct epoch or step.

annotations.title: Model state
annotations.explanation: The current learned parameters and persistent buffers must be restored.

annotations.title: Optimizer state
annotations.explanation: Momentum and adaptive optimizers maintain internal state beyond model weights.

annotations.title: Scheduler state
annotations.explanation: If the learning-rate schedule has internal progress, save it for a seamless resume.

prompts.label: WEIGHTS-ONLY IS DIFFERENT FROM RESUMABLE TRAINING
prompts.placeholder: When are model weights alone insufficient?

reveal.text: Model weights can be enough for inference, but a seamless training resume may also require optimizer, scheduler, scaler, epoch/step, and other experiment state.

prompts.label: PUT FORWARD AND LOSS INSIDE AUTOCAST
prompts.placeholder: Click autocast and notice that backward stays outside the context.

reveal.code:
optimizer.zero_grad()

with torch.autocast(
    device_type="cuda",
    dtype=torch.float16,
):
    logits = model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(logits, y)

loss.backward()
optimizer.step()

annotations.title: Automatic mixed precision context
annotations.explanation: Eligible forward/loss operations use selected lower precision while other operations remain in higher precision as appropriate.

annotations.title: Loss computed inside autocast
annotations.explanation: The forward pass and loss computation belong inside the autocast region.

annotations.title: Backward outside autocast
annotations.explanation: Do not put backward itself inside autocast; backward uses dtypes associated with the recorded forward operations.

prompts.label: SCALE LOSS, STEP THROUGH THE SCALER, THEN UPDATE
prompts.placeholder: Click GradScaler and the three scaler operations.

reveal.code:
scaler = torch.amp.GradScaler("cuda")

optimizer.zero_grad()

with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
    logits = model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(logits, y)

scaler.scale(loss).backward()
scaler.step(optimizer)
scaler.update()

annotations.title: Create a CUDA gradient scaler
annotations.explanation: GradScaler helps reduce float16 gradient underflow during mixed-precision training.

annotations.title: Scale before backward
annotations.explanation: The scaler multiplies the loss so small float16 gradients are less likely to underflow.

annotations.title: Conditionally perform optimizer step
annotations.explanation: The scaler unscales/checks gradients as part of the step workflow and can skip invalid updates.

annotations.title: Update the scaling factor
annotations.explanation: The scaler adjusts its scale for subsequent iterations.

prompts.label: GRADSCALER IS NOT FOR EVERY MODE

reveal.text: It is not required for ordinary full-precision training and is not needed for inference-only autocast.

prompts.label: COMPILE, THEN CALL NORMALLY
prompts.placeholder: Click torch.compile and the ordinary model call.

reveal.code:
import torch

compiled_model = torch.compile(model)

for X, y in loader:
    logits = compiled_model(X)
    loss = loss_fn(logits, y)

annotations.title: Wrap the model with compilation
annotations.explanation: torch.compile returns an optimized callable backed by PyTorch compilation infrastructure.

annotations.title: Use it like the original model
annotations.explanation: After compilation, call the compiled model through the normal Python interface.

prompts.label: COMPILE PERFORMANCE MUST BE MEASURED
prompts.placeholder: Why can compile fail to improve a workload?

reveal.text: Compilation can add startup overhead and graph breaks, so measure end-to-end performance rather than assuming every workload becomes faster.

prompts.label: RECORD THE EXPERIMENT CONTROLS
prompts.placeholder: Click the seeds and deterministic-algorithm setting.

reveal.code:
import random
import torch

seed = 42

random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(seed)

torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)

annotations.title: Seed Python's RNG
annotations.explanation: Reproducible experiments may need multiple random-number generators seeded, not only PyTorch.

annotations.title: Seed PyTorch RNGs
annotations.explanation: This starts PyTorch random-number generation from a known seed.

annotations.title: Request deterministic algorithms
annotations.explanation: Where supported, PyTorch can require deterministic algorithm choices rather than nondeterministic alternatives.

prompts.label: EXACT REPRODUCIBILITY HAS LIMITS
prompts.placeholder: Is bit-for-bit reproducibility guaranteed across releases and platforms?

reveal.text: No. Exact reproducibility is not guaranteed across PyTorch releases, platforms, or all CPU and accelerator operations. Record software versions, data splits, seeds, and hyperparameters when comparing experiments.
